clauses.reason: The order states that EO 12834 "is hereby revoked, effective at noon January 20, 2001". The revocation executed itself at that moment, so the command was exhausted by performance on 2001-01-20; its consequence (EO 12834 remains revoked and the commitments no longer bind) survives as an accrued effect and is not a continuing command. No earlier end is held and no held later instrument names this order.

research_rationale:
EO 13184 (signed 2000-12-28; 66 FR 697, Federal Register of 2001-01-03, FR Doc. 01-255) was read in full in the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13184.txt. Its single command revokes EO 12834 of January 20, 1993 (Ethics Commitments by Executive Branch Appointees), effective at noon January 20, 2001, and states that employees and former employees subject to the commitments in EO 12834 will not be subject to them after the effective date. The revocation is self-executing: it was performed by operation of the order at its stated effective moment, so the single clause is exhausted by performance on 2001-01-20. The consequence (EO 12834 stays revoked) survives as an accrued effect; it is not a continuing command of EO 13184. A by-number search of held order texts finds no later order citing EO 13184, and the three machine searches record no amendment, revocation or supersession. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the official Federal Register PDF; the PDF page images are not held, so identity (printed number, title, signing date and FR Doc. number) was checked on the text layer against the census register row.

savings.reason: The order has no savings clause. Its consequence, that EO 12834 and the commitments under it no longer bind after noon January 20, 2001, is an accrued effect of the completed revocation and requires no further action by the order. No held source shows any pending matter, exception or later reinstatement of EO 12834 by an instrument naming EO 13184.
